skill.name: stop-slop
skill.description: Edits durable prose to remove machine-written patterns while preserving facts, technical content, useful contrasts, and the author's voice.
skill.summary: Make durable prose sound specific, natural, and consistent with its original voice.

content.user_title: Remove Machine-Written Tells from Durable Prose
content.value_statement: Durable prose can sound generic when rhetoric obscures concrete facts. This skill removes formulaic patterns while preserving meaning, technical details, and voice.
actual_capabilities: Identifies rhetorical framing, manufactured contrasts, decorative triads, dramatic setups, and uniform sentence rhythm.
Rewrites marked prose while preserving facts, code, commands, tables, data, and quoted material.
Uses representative source paragraphs to match sentence length, comment density, idiom, and tone.
Applies direct language, consistent terminology, focused paragraphs, and practical procedural sentence limits.
Checks lexical warning signs after addressing higher-impact structural patterns.
limitations: It is intended for durable artifacts, not ordinary chat replies or progress updates.
It does not verify factual accuracy or add missing technical information.
It needs representative source text to match a specific author or product voice.
Its default mechanics favor plain ASCII and may conflict with another publication style guide.

use_cases.title: Refine Product Documentation
use_cases.description: Remove generic framing from guides and README files while preserving commands, procedures, and technical facts.

use_cases.title: Polish Release Communication
use_cases.description: Make release notes and pull request text direct, specific, and consistent with the team voice.

use_cases.title: Improve Interface Copy
use_cases.description: Rewrite labels, messages, and supporting text without changing product behavior or user expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Clean Up a Paragraph
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this paragraph to remove machine-written patterns. Preserve every fact and keep the existing tone: [paste paragraph]
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a focused edit of one paragraph.

prompt_templates.title: Revise Technical Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise this documentation for direct, natural prose. Preserve code, commands, tables, quoted text, and all technical details: [paste document]
prompt_templates.scenario: A writer needs a complete documentation pass.

prompt_templates.title: Match an Established Voice
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the sample as a voice anchor, then revise the draft. Match its sentence length, idiom, and density without copying phrases. Sample: [text] Draft: [text]
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants new copy to match an existing voice.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Explain Editorial Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this artifact for structural writing patterns. Rewrite only justified cases, preserve useful contrasts, and summarize which facts and technical elements remained unchanged: [paste artifact]
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a transparent editorial review.

output_examples.input: Rewrite: Our robust platform empowers teams to unlock seamless collaboration across today's evolving landscape.
output_examples.output: The platform gives teams one workspace for sharing drafts, assigning reviews, and tracking approvals.

output_examples.input: Rewrite without losing the behavior: The service fails honestly. It does not pretend that unfinished checks passed.
output_examples.output: An unfinished check returns block instead of pass.

output_examples.input: Review this real contrast: Gates block, advisors comment.
output_examples.output: Keep it. Each clause names a distinct behavior, so the contrast adds information.

best_practices: Provide two or three representative paragraphs when the result must match an established voice.
State which facts, terminology, code, commands, tables, and quotations must remain unchanged.
Review the complete result for meaning and sentence variation before publishing it.
anti_patterns: Do not request broad shortening when every fact must remain present.
Do not remove every contrast, fragment, or expressive sentence without checking its purpose.
Do not use the skill to rewrite code, data, commands, or third-party quotations.

faq.question: What types of text should I provide?
faq.answer: Use documentation, README files, release notes, interface copy, comments, commit messages, pull requests, or issue text.

faq.question: Does the skill change technical meaning?
faq.answer: It aims to preserve every fact and technical element. You should still review important artifacts before publication.

faq.question: Can it match my existing voice?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide two or three representative paragraphs from the same author or product.

faq.question: Does it remove every flagged phrase?
faq.answer: No. A phrase is a review prompt, and useful wording remains when it carries real information.

faq.question: Will it edit code and commands?
faq.answer: No. The workflow preserves code, commands, data, tables, and quoted third-party material.

faq.question: Does it enforce Simplified Technical English?
faq.answer: It follows those principles loosely. It applies the controlled dictionary only when the user requests strict compliance.
